                                  D ECISION
         In accordance with 16 Texas Administrative Code § 22.261(d) and the exceptions-and-re-
plies memorandum in this proceeding, the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners timely
file these exceptions to the proposal for decision (“PFD”). 1 The Administrative Law Judges’
(“ALJs’”) thorough, 196-page PFD in this proceeding is well-reasoned and presents little cause
for objection. So the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners’ exceptions are brief. And gen-
erally, the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners support the PFD.

                                  I.       Routing Criteria (Issues 8–10)
         The M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners’ exceptions relate solely to the routing-
criteria issues—specifically the PFD’s descriptions of the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Land-
owners’ positions on three of the five routes that the ALJs describe as the “Other Routes.” 2
         First, the PFD states that “Route 891 is a Central Corridor route supported by the Sneeds
and opposed by the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners.” 3 But the M31, M32, and M33

M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners’ Exceptions to the Proposal for Decision                            1 of 4
 Opposition Landowners do not oppose Route 891. 4 Instead, the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition
Landowners view Route 891 as an acceptable alternative to Route 894. 5
        Second, the PFD describes Route 572 as being “opposed by Williamson County and New-
man Group.” 6 The M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners also oppose Route 572 for many
of the same reasons that the ALJs disfavor the route: “Route 572 is $8.3 million more expensive,
2.5 miles longer, has less paralleling, and impacts 22 more habitable structures than Route 894.” 7
        And third, the PFD states that Route CCG “is opposed by the Gainer Family, G6 Landown-
ers Legal Fund, Yates Keith Alliance, and Newman Group.” 8 The M31, M32, and M33 Opposition
Landowners also oppose Route CCG. As the PFD rightly observes, “[c]ompared to any of the
Focus Routes, Route CCG is 3.17 miles longer and approximately $40 million more expensive.” 9
And “Route CCG has 105 habitable structures within 500 feet of the centerline, which is 20 more
than Route 894 and nine more than Route 487.” 10 Also, the “different San Saba River crossing”11
that Route CCG uses “creates a single point of failure for multiple transmission lines at the San
Saba River crossing by locating the Project right next to AEP Texas’s existing Mason-to-North
Brady transmission line.” 12
        Of course, the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners acknowledge that these ex-
ceptions are relatively unimportant because “[n]one of these routes present a clear advantage over
the Focus Routes overall such that it should be given serious consideration as the route selected
for the Project.” 13 The M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners agree with the ALJs on that
point and present these exceptions only to enhance the PFD’s accuracy.




        4
           See, e.g., M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners’ Initial Br. at 3 (Jun. 19, 2026) (“Alternatively, if
the ALJs and the Commission don’t agree that Route 894 best meets the statutory and regulatory routing factors, the
M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners also do not oppose Routes 487 or 891.”); M31, M32, and M33
Opposition Landowners’ Reply Br. at 2 (Jun. 26, 2026) (“[T]he M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners also do
not oppose Routes 487, 891, or 894 Western Mod. 1.”).
